key_insight: OSCAR turns LLM-based optimization modeling into a staged search process: generate, simulate, and escalate to stronger models only when needed to certify better solutions.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical way to produce locally runnable, lower-cost optimization formulations while reducing the risk that an LLM returns a correct answer to the wrong problem.
method: Simulator validates candidates against labeled feasible/infeasible decision examples.
Coder and Reviewer roles generate and check formulations, then search beyond mere feasibility for certified improvement.
Cost-ordered escalation allocates attempts across models and stopping rules to balance price, capability, and confidence.
evidence_signal: On five benchmark problems, OSCAR reached 95%–100% accuracy with two small open-weight local models, while single-attempt accuracies averaged 29% and 48%; Codex and Claude Code used 3.1× and 5.8× more tokens on average over five runs.
watch_item: Performance depends on having labeled decision examples and a reliable simulator, so setup effort and label quality may limit deployment in new domains.
paper_title: OR for AI That Does OR: Routing LLMs up the Escalator inside the OSCAR Framework
